VERDICT: REJECT

The proposed answer of 0 rests on the claim that every positive integer is the order of some finite partisan misère quotient. The argument for this is only a gesture: it says partisan games are "flexible enough" and gives no construction for any order beyond 2. The problem also presupposes that some positive integers are not realizable, since it asks for their sum. I recall that the literature on partisan misère quotients (Carvalho, Huggan, Morrison, Neilson and coauthors) identifies specific orders that cannot occur, so the sum should be positive. I could not verify the exact set of exceptions, so I have not computed the correct sum.

CONFIDENCE: 3
